candidates.why: Must Read: controlled decomposition of chain-completion collapse (authorship vs verification) over 280 chains x 10 agents x 8 attempts with clustered CIs, cross-model-review paired twins, contamination and harness checks, and full artifact release - the most rigorous agent-reliability evidence this week.
candidates.caveat: Specifications are model-written and model-audited, not human-reviewed, and the 51% chain-completion headline is an upper bound (strict pass@1 is 39%).

candidates.why: Prospective wet-lab validation in two domains is exceptional, but the 15.9% vs 8.7% hit-rate comparison is cross-campaign rather than randomized (n=2-3 replicates, weak-baseline caveats), and BOBA already carries this area with higher-powered controlled evidence.
candidates.caveat: The prospective hit-rate comparison (15.9% vs 8.7%) is a cross-campaign comparison rather than a randomized head-to-head - the two workflows picked different compounds from the same library, and a single 107-compound campaign has wide uncertainty.

candidates.why: Preregistered, hashed predictions and 411 controlled loops are exemplary science, but scope is two environments x one harm each x four safeguards, with GEPA and natural loops explicitly case studies - strong, edged out within its area by BOBA's sample size and breadth.
candidates.caveat: Most loops are planted single deletions; natural loops (18) and GEPA (3 seeds, few harm events) are explicitly 'case studies, not estimates', and the headline GEPA seed-2 effect is p=.003 by run-level Fisher but only p=.125 by task-level sign test.

candidates.why: Must Read: clean causal intervention (LM-head precision: 0/5 FP32 vs 5/5 BF16 failures at 5 seeds), direct quantization-error instrumentation, a negative control (fixed softmax), and a practical one-line LM-head SGD-M fix, with code released.
candidates.caveat: Spikes are elicited with learning rates up to 3e-1 - 1-2 orders of magnitude above production-scale LRs - and a natural-LR, >=7B demonstration is absent.

candidates.why: 99.5% spike-burden reduction is striking and honestly reported, but it rests on 3 seeds at 1.31B tokens with no uniform-scaling control, so energy-dependent attenuation versus plain update shrinkage is unresolved.
candidates.caveat: The cleaner Cohort M (matched LR/WD) still lacks the routed-only uniform-scaling control the author himself flags - a fixed q~0.96 baseline would test whether energy-dependent assignment matters at all.

candidates.why: Decisive, well-instrumented negative result for label-free monitoring, but everything rests on one synthetic generator with a reduced two-view LeJEPA recipe - possibly a pathology of the author's own minimal setup rather than SSL generally.
candidates.caveat: External validity is the main weakness: one synthetic physics generator, a 0.7M ViT-Nano, and a REDUCED two-view recipe - this may be a pathology specific to the author's minimal recipe, not LeJEPA or SSL generally.

candidates.why: Must Read: identifies a mechanism-level invisible failure (0.4-0.5% of served weights change per step; hidden ratio invisible to every deployed diagnostic), validated with 25 matched seed-pairs, an fp32-sampler oracle, a controls battery, and an adversarial self-ablation showing unbiased export alone collapses.
candidates.caveat: Several configurations are single-seed and by the authors' own numbers many endpoint differences are within noise - the +6.1 mean and 18/6/1 record lean on the logic-task tail, at <=4B scale and 150-500 steps.

candidates.why: Careful discrepancy/lag decomposition with good measurement hygiene (paired on-policy references, noise floors, 3 seeds), but the evidence envelope is 40 steps, one task, one optimizer, and DLC ties or trails IS+centering at 0.6B and 8B.
candidates.caveat: Tiny experimental envelope: 40 training steps, Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B, one task (Countdown with +/-1 rewards), one optimizer (SGD, lr 1e-2) - DLC does not dominate, its clearest win is the 1.7B regime where plain IS collapses.

candidates.why: Pure theory: the no-free-lunch and crossing theorems are conditional on stylized assumptions never verified on any real workload, and the only empirical input is one transcribed published table - formalization here is not validation.
candidates.caveat: The two load-bearing assumptions - exclusive/dominant specialization and fine coverage of the hardest prompts - are never verified on any real model's evaluation log, even though the paper's own diagnostic could in principle test them.

candidates.why: Valuable industrial experience with two striking production intercepts, but as evidence it has no controlled evaluation - no per-stage bug attribution, no reported false-positive rate, and nothing verifiable outside Google's proprietary stack.
candidates.caveat: There is no head-to-head comparison against prior fuzzing tools, no bug-discovery-rate metric per stage, and - most conspicuously - no ablation attributing the 142 bugs to the three fuzzing stages, and the pipeline's own false-positive rate is never reported.

candidates.why: Well-controlled plug-in evaluation (independent labeling, 92% vs 83%/55% component ablation, disclosed false-rejection rate), but on a compact attention-heavy 39-task suite with one LLM and one GPU, and end-to-end severity of violations is asserted, not measured.
candidates.caveat: Evaluation is kernel-level: no end-to-end measurement of how residual batch variance propagates to generated tokens, evaluation scores, or serving behavior, and passing the finite dynamic sweep is evidence, not proof (8.1% of finals still violate).

candidates.why: Must Read: a complete causal chain - bit-exact FP8 GEMM emulator validated on all 168 captures, single-projection arithmetic bisection, matched-perturbation controls separating structure from magnitude, and application-level recovery (AUROC 0.434 to 0.869, paired CI) with hashed plans and a per-number provenance ledger.
candidates.caveat: mmaemu's bit-exactness is validated only on 1B captures - all 40B conclusions ride on an extrapolated model, and the 1.4% shrinkage gain is fitted in-sample, so the mechanism claim is a diagnostic, not established.

candidates.why: Exemplary audit craftsmanship (tight 14.998C witness, causal forced-mask localization, four matched controls), but the natural-data excess is 6.5% on one OPT-125M batch and the 2M-draw release audit detects no violation of the advertised guarantee - real premise flaw, modest demonstrated harm.
candidates.caveat: The natural-data excess is 6.5% on OPT-125M - the smallest model in the relevant family - and the 2M-draw audit finds no violation of the advertised epsilon; no currently shipping default configuration is shown vulnerable end-to-end.

candidates.why: Must Read: a provable iff-condition (block-exponent spread <= 3) turned into a deployed, bit-identical W4A8 system - propositions proved, 0 of 298M packed weights differ, McNemar-tested GSM8K 94.8% vs 91.0% on a 125B MoE, and honest reporting of where it loses (decode).
candidates.caveat: All numbers come from one M5 Max on macOS 26.6, decode is never improved (0.90-1.01x MLX; the 16-block format decodes at 0.65x), and rotations+GPTQ under the spread constraint was not tested.

candidates.why: Genuinely careful measurement design (paired-prompt bootstrap CIs, break-even model validated four ways, C1-C7 guards, 108 fault-injection tests), but every arm is single-seed over 10-60 steps and the main dense results ran with a self-disclosed half-matched-sampler bug.
candidates.caveat: The dense vLLM arms of settings A and B were affected by the F2 bug - gate_up_proj (52% of each decoder layer's linear weights) stayed in BF16 - so the main dense MXFP8/MXFP8 results are for a half-matched sampler, reported 'as run'.

candidates.why: Must Read: converts an observational interpretability claim into an exact A+C-D decomposition with a neuron-level mechanism (closed-gate leak), causal annealing interventions (cosine -0.184 to +0.021 vs -0.170 control) across 16 models, pre-registered controls, and honest reproduction of the prior number.
candidates.caveat: The main measurements rest on sixteen 192-token FineWeb-Edu documents, models are capped at 8B, and selectivity is refuted at the direction level only - feature-level selectivity is left open.

candidates.why: Mechanism-first design with clean target-swap ablations and consistent gains across families and 14B, but single-author, no code release, and the two non-Qwen model families rest on 100-case splits - strong, just short of Must Read in a competitive week.
candidates.caveat: Main tables for Llama-3 and Qwen3 use only 100 two-hop cases (vs 300 for Qwen2.5), so per-model deltas like 0.62 vs 0.51 carry nontrivial noise, and locality trails AlphaEdit (Nbr 0.66 vs 0.98).

candidates.why: Textbook causal-intervention methodology (removal, transplant, state transplant triangulate one conclusion) with cross-architecture block replacement, but every claim rests on an 8-pair single-token synthetic lookup - no long-context or naturalistic retrieval evidence.
candidates.caveat: Evidence is confined to a synthetic 8-entry, single-token key-value task; no needle-in-a-haystack, multi-hop, or natural-document retrieval is tested, so transfer to realistic long-context retrieval is asserted by framing rather than tested.

candidates.why: Exceptionally open artifact with real per-module quantization forensics, but the numbers are self-reported and mid-pack on its flagship agentic benchmarks (SWE-bench Pro 51.78 vs DS-V4 72.00; Terminal-Bench -25 pts) - a deployable artifact, not a Must Read.
candidates.caveat: The headline 'surpassing Nemotron 3 Ultra' comparator is NVIDIA's own previous generation, while the same table shows DS-V4 Flash-0731 beating Super by 20+ points on SWE-bench Pro - the abstract does not surface this.

candidates.why: Genuinely independent, version-over-version, execution-trace-grounded evaluation - but GLM-5.3 simultaneously simulates users, persuades, and judges many suites, and the in-house benchmarks carrying the worst regressions (LoCBench 12%) are unreleased, so the most novel results cannot be checked.
candidates.caveat: GLM-5.3 serves simultaneously as simulated user, persuader, and judge on many conversational suites - the report concedes this 'may introduce bias, especially when evaluating conversations it helped generate'.

candidates.why: Strong ablation hygiene and honest negative baselines, but headline deltas inflate against near-zero diffusion baselines and the unified-DLLM field is young - best-in-class within a niche rather than a Must Read.
candidates.caveat: The 'delta vs Diff. SOTA' row takes the max per column across heterogeneous baselines of very different sizes, inflating deltas like ScreenSpot-Pro +48.8 over a baseline that scores 0.4 there.

candidates.why: Must Read: defines, measures at scale (91,469 production calls + 89,047 public trajectories + 8 harnesses), and repairs a real failure mode with a TLA+-model-checked fix - false successes cut 73.5% with task-paired CIs, 85% detection at zero false positives, deployed at 0.54 ms median overhead.
candidates.caveat: The Terminus-2 headline (25/25, 0 false successes) rests on single runs, and the production corpus (6 developers, one company) is unreleased, so the real-world anchor cannot be independently verified.

candidates.why: Best-in-genre external validation (32 new defects, 21 maintainer confirmations, 18 upstream fixes including Anthropic's SDK), but recall is an in-sample upper bound mined from the same 120 fixes and the single-site model excludes 24/120 known defect classes - strong second in a one-star area.
candidates.caveat: The 0.78 recall is an in-sample upper bound - the detection rules were mined from the same 120 fixes - and the held-out 571-repo study reports precision only, with no recall denominator.

candidates.why: Useful measurement with a deployable heuristic trio, but the detector bake-off's pre-registered protocol effectively failed (no reader met the <=5% false-alarm bar; conclusion salvaged by re-interpretation) and all rates come from one vantage point over 3 days.
candidates.caveat: The primary protocol comparison effectively failed: no content reader met the <=5% realized false-alarm requirement on the reviewed sample, and the 'cheap heuristics win' conclusion rests on a protocol re-interpretation honestly disclosed in Appendix C.

candidates.why: Must Read: real 64-GPU training gains (up to 27.1% step time on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 6.0% over FSDP2+SymmMem with paired-t CIs excluding zero) backed by a 239-config correctness suite, 41 fault-injection tests, bitwise determinism, and a from-scratch convergence-parity run.
candidates.caveat: The paper's own design-space table names NCCL PACE as the closest prior system, yet PACE never appears in the end-to-end comparisons, and the 27.1% headline picks the best model/shape cell (3.1% for dense Llama at 32K).

candidates.why: Careful kernel engineering with full ablations and a 792-cell shape sweep, but the 4.14x headline rides a weak-baseline layout quirk (1.10-1.80x against the stronger Splash-Attention) and accuracy validation is thin relative to the numerical risk taken (BF16 inverse, 20-sample v7x checks).
candidates.caveat: The 4.14x headline is against RPA-v3, whose MHA layout wastes half of each BF16 register - against the stronger Splash-Attention the kernel-only gain is 1.10-1.80x and the full-block gain only 1.01-1.15x.

candidates.why: Honest, well-controlled kernel work (FP32 reference checks, competitor engines strengthened with the authors' own decomposition), but the advertised maxima come from degenerate baseline paths and there is no LLM-scale evaluation - solid, not Must Read.
candidates.caveat: The advertised ranges (up to 21x backward, up to 128x memory, up to 228x vs decomposition-augmented engines) are dominated by degenerate baselines - the honest per-mechanism floor is TXL's 1.8x/2.0x.
